brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Teal/amber dual-organism color coding immediately communicates healthy vs stressed states without needing labels
Dark canvas with luminous orbs creates a tactile, almost biological visceral pull aligned with the brief
Numeric hierarchy (giant percentage, small caption) reads cleanly at a glance from across the room
dominant_weaknesses: Orbs are static spheres in a still image — the entire 'breathes vs pulses' premise lives in motion that isn't shown or implied
Bottom four metric cards are generic dashboard tiles, breaking the organism metaphor and feeling pasted from another design
Massive empty space around each orb wastes canvas without adding ambient detail, satellites, or rhythm cues
fix_priorities: Commit to the metaphor: add motion specs, breathing halos, particle orbits, or waveform pulses tied to load
Redesign bottom row as smaller organism satellites or vital-sign sparklines instead of flat KPI cards
Tighten orb containers and add ambient texture (veins, membrane, ECG ring) so the spheres feel alive at rest
Refine typography — the percent and label weights are conventional; a more organic or medical typeface would deepen voice
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral appeal from the glowing orbs, but behavioral payoff is thin (no live rhythm) and reflective meaning stops at color-coding.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the visual language hints at organisms, but without visible motion or biological detail it reads as a stylized gauge dashboard rather than living creatures.
